content.text: {"count": 2, "rationale": "Deploying mfa:admin and mfa:dbadmin together blocks exfiltration, and no single control does. Every exfiltration path ends at admin on db, fileserver or backup. Reaching any of them requires the matching auth step, which needs stolen_dbadmin and either NOT mfa_dbadmin or admin on dc/adfs. Why two controls are needed without blocking the internal network: phishing always gives foothold_workstation and stolen_user, and mfa:user does not stop the auth steps when foothold_workstation holds. So the attacker can reach appserver, apiserver or ciserver and kerberoast stolen_admin. With stolen_admin, escalate_ciserver ignores patching, and leak_secrets_ciserver yields stolen_dbadmin. Patching db, fileserver or backup does nothing, because their escalation needs no unpatched condition. Why the pair works: mfa:dbadmin forces the need for admin on dc or adfs, and mfa:admin blocks auth_dc and auth_adfs, so neither can be gained. The three exfiltration auth steps therefore can never fire. Why no single control works: with only mfa:dbadmin, auth_dc leads to admin_dc, which bypasses it. With only mfa:admin, stolen_dbadmin from ciserver lets auth_db proceed. With only segmented, escalate_workstation still enables pivot_internal. Any single patch is bypassed through another host or through stolen_admin. Blocking reach_internal instead would take three controls (segmented, patched:workstation, patched:laptop), so the minimum is 2."}
